fixer.summary:
I added `Combat.spend_movement(c, cost, what, *, page, rule, ruling=None, free_off_turn=False)` in dungdra/combat.py, and both move() and stand_up() now use it. It is now the only place that checks the turn, compares the cost with `movement_left`, refuses and subtracts the movement. Following R-22, it refuses before changing anything if the full cost isn't left.

The ticket also asked me to decide what voluntary movement off the creature's own turn means. Movement is a budget of a creature's own turn, so off-turn the helper refuses by default, and stand_up() keeps that behaviour (it now also cites R-22). move() passes `free_off_turn=True`, so off-turn moves go ahead without touching the current turn's budget. I didn't make move() refuse too because a voluntary off-turn move is legitimate: the acceptance scenario test_cmb04_controlled_mount_provokes moves a controlled mount on its rider's turn. When I tried refusing in move() as well, that scenario failed.

Two smaller changes in move():
- `turn.moved` and the "ft left" note in the log now depend on whether the budget was actually spent.
- I removed the unused `jump` parameter. It was only read in the old no-op branch, and nothing passes it; vulture flagged it once that branch was gone.

The over-budget refusal from move() now reads "Moving N ft costs X ft of movement; <name> has Y ft left". No test matched the old wording.

Results: the full suite has 697 passed and 33 xfailed, and the unit tests pass. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean, and dev-gate passes (dead_code is back to 3). The ticket listed no acceptance tests, so there were none to run with `--runxfail`.

followups.title: dungdra/combat.py move(): off-turn voluntary movement is still unbudgeted (free_off_turn=True for every caller). Decide which off-turn moves are legitimate (controlled mount, reaction-granted movement) and refuse the rest through spend_movement, proposing a ruling if the SRD is silent
